solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Before one caught European breaking mug made of pottery

indicators.note: the first part is placed before the letters for one and caught
the European letter breaks into the word for mug, splitting it open

parts.note: to mug up is to cram, to study hard in a rush
the Roman numeral I stands for one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone describes a broken mug in a European kitchen before it was caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' sets CERAM ahead of I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramic ware is fired clay, so a ceramic object is one fashioned from pottery.

clue.text: Amundsen's fate — Hobson's choice of where to turn from the south pole?

parts.note: N, north, is the direction to head
Hobson's choice is no choice at all, so the offer is one thing OR the very same thing
standing at the south pole every direction is N, north

explanation.surface: A musing on the explorer Amundsen at the South Pole, where his only option was to head back.
explanation.walkthrough: At the south pole every way out is north, so the 'choice' is north or north: N OR N. Hobson's choice means taking the one thing offered or nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth the three Fates are called Norns, and Amundsen was a Norwegian, so his fate is a Norse one.

clue.text: Almost sick after fast pulse

indicators.note: the shortened word for sick comes after the season of fasting

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

indicators.note: almost signals that the final letter of the word for sick is dropped

parts.note: sick means ill

explanation.surface: Someone feels nearly ill after a period of fasting, their pulse affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes such as peas, beans and this small lens-shaped seed.

clue.text: Bad press corporation is trapped in more than one tough inquiry?

indicators.note: the belly word is shut inside the rearranged letters of press
bad suggests the letters of press are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a media corporation caught by awkward questions from a hostile press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' gives SPERS; 'corporation' is an old joke word for a pot belly. The question mark flags the plural definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumper is a puzzling question that baffles, so several difficult queries are plural of it.

clue.text: Charge about to subdue old film, one analysing the class system?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first part sits on top of the rest, holding it down

parts.note: a tax is a charge levied
on means about, as in a talk on a subject
a film of moisture is a mist

explanation.surface: An old film is suppressed by a fee, and someone studies the social class system.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer TAXON sits over OMIST, the picture behind 'to subdue'. The 'class system' is biological classes, not social ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxonomist classifies organisms into groups such as class, order and genus.

clue.text: Hard to grasp scoop Times initially chucked out

indicators.note: out signals these letters are removed from the word for scoop

parts.note: a scoop is a newspaper exclusive
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of chucked

explanation.surface: A newspaper's exclusive story proves slippery after The Times throws it out.
explanation.walkthrough: Take XC (X for times, C from 'chucked') out of EXCLUSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elusive slips away, evading capture or understanding, so it is hard to get hold of.

clue.text: Rescue one who wanders around city

indicators.note: the wanderer is placed around the city letters

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A wanderer roaming about a city mounts a rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: EC, the City of London's postal district, is standard crossword shorthand for city.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue something is to get it back, retrieving or reclaiming what was lost.

clue.text: Religious artefact in Last Supper only half sculpted

indicators.note: sculpted means shaped anew, so the letters are remodelled
only half takes the first three of the six letters of Supper

explanation.surface: A religious work showing the Last Supper is left only half carved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half' gives SUP from Supper; 'sculpted' rearranges LAST SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Wren's London cathedral is a man-made religious building, loosely an artefact.

clue.text: Straight railway with damaged erratic banking

indicators.note: the rearranged letters bank, flank, the railway on both sides
damaged signals the letters of erratic are broken up and reordered

parts.note: a railway line, so line stands for railway

explanation.surface: A damaged straight railway line with erratic cambered curves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' rearranges ERRATIC to RECTIAR, which banks LINE on either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectilinear figures are bounded by straight lines, so the word describes something straight.

clue.text: Normal raiments patched up by mother

indicators.note: the mother's letters stand by, next to, the rest

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: patched up suggests the letters of raiments are mended into new order

explanation.surface: Mum mends a child's ordinary clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patched up' makes INSTREAM; raiments are clothes, which is what gives the surface its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream ideas or tastes are conventional, those of the majority, hence ordinary.

clue.text: More or less dislodge lid from trunk

indicators.note: the lid is the top, first letter of the word for trunk, which is knocked off

parts.note: the trunk of the body is the torso

explanation.surface: Instructions to prise the lid off a trunk, give or take.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived idiom or so means approximately, roughly that amount, give or take.

clue.text: It can be scheduled by destiny

parts.note: by in measurements, as in three by four, means times
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Something that may be arranged by fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is multiplication, three by four meaning three times four.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot in a timetable is a period booked for something, the thing a schedule allocates.

clue.text: Call up head touring Channel Islands for free

indicators.note: the joined letters go round the islands' abbreviation, enclosing it
in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
pate is an old word for the head
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands, off France

explanation.surface: Someone is summoned by a boss travelling around the Channel Islands for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads from the bottom, giving EMAN; 'Call up' as a phrase misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: To emancipate is to liberate, setting people at liberty from slavery or restriction.

clue.text: Develop fondness about heartless vedette

indicators.note: about signals that the fondness word turns round

parts.note: love is fondness

indicators.note: heartless removes everything between the first and last letters of vedette

explanation.surface: A fondness grows for a star performer who is cold at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns LOVE to EVOL; 'heartless' leaves VE from vedette. A vedette is a leading actress or star.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to unfold gradually, growing into a more advanced form.

clue.text: Destructive spiteful woman with icy calm ordered around son

parts.note: a cat is slang for a spiteful woman

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the son's letter
ordered says the letters of icy calm are arranged afresh

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman, calm as ice, wreaks havoc around her son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges ICY CALM, and those letters go 'around' S to make ACLYSMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a violent upheaval or disaster, so the adjective means ruinous.

clue.text: Universities backed intended financial qualification

parts.note: ACA, Associate Chartered Accountant, is a UK accounting qualification

indicators.note: backed means set going backwards, so the word for intended is reversed

parts.note: aimed means intended, as in aimed to please

explanation.surface: Universities supported a planned finance qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' gives DEMIA, which in the answer follows the qualification even though the clue names it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of higher learning and scholarship, the collective realm of universities.

clue.text: Bucolic English record interrupting signal

indicators.note: the record word breaks into the signal word

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act
a log is a record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: A rustic English recording is cut off by a signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucolic is used here as a noun, a pastoral poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral poem about shepherds is called a bucolic, Virgil's being the classic examples.

clue.text: One in eight I'd put back inside? That's more disturbing

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the oarsman word

parts.note: a rowing eight has eight oarsmen, each a rower

indicators.note: put back means the two letters are reversed

explanation.surface: Someone says they'd put one of eight items back inside, and wonders whether that is more upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, so 'one in eight' is an oarsman, not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdier is the comparative of rowdy, noisier and more unruly, causing more disturbance.

clue.text: First-rate accountant about to turn round plant

indicators.note: the whole string is turned round, reading from right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
CA is a chartered accountant
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A top accountant is about to turn round a plant business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To turn round' reverses AICACA.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub, the wattle, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Volunteers to stop people swimming

indicators.note: the volunteers' letters plug, stop up, the people word

parts.note: a nation is a people
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers are sent to stop people swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Natation is a formal word for the act or art of swimming, from Latin natare.

clue.text: Dainty bird (a young woman, crudely)

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
bit is a crude slang word for a young woman, as in a bit of stuff

explanation.surface: A delicate little bird, or a young woman in crude slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A dainty is a choice morsel or delicacy, the same sense as a tasty treat.

clue.text: Ceremony, mass, held by father

indicators.note: the mass letter is held inside the father word

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A ceremony and mass presided over by a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a priest but means POP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomp is ceremonial splendour and display, the trappings of a grand ceremony.

clue.text: Attention to detail in middle of next organised audit, etc

indicators.note: middle of takes the central two letters of next
organised says the letters of audit and etc are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fussy precision at the heart of the next well-run audit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of' takes EX from next; 'organised' rearranges AUDIT ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactitude is precision, carefulness and accuracy in small things.

clue.text: Pulled broadcast of what lecturer did

indicators.note: broadcast signals a word spoken out loud that sounds like another

parts.note: a lecturer teaches, so what one did was taught

explanation.surface: A lecture transmission was pulled from the schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope pulled tight is stretched and tense, with no slack.

clue.text: UCU once hosting small display around country

indicators.note: the old union's letters host, hold within, the small letter

parts.note: the University and College Union was formed partly from the AUT, the Association of University Teachers

indicators.note: around means the display word turns round

parts.note: to air something is to display it

explanation.surface: A lecturers' union once staged a small exhibition about a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: UCU is Britain's University and College Union, created in 2006 by merging the AUT with another lecturers' union, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a nation of central Europe, capital Vienna.

clue.text: Idle suspicion is late for circulation

indicators.note: circulation means going round, so the word for late circles the slang word

parts.note: the late person has died
sus is British slang for suspicion, as in arrested on sus

explanation.surface: An idle suspicion is too late to be passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is only a link; 'for circulation' has the word for late going round the slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery that is idle has fallen out of use, abandoned and no longer employed.
